subtopics.title: Current — Counting Charge Past a Point

questions.question: Electric current is defined as:
options: The energy carried by a battery
The rate of flow of charge, $I = Q/\Delta t$
The number of electrons in a wire

questions.question: A kettle element passes 300 C of charge in 40 s. The current is:
A torch bulb carries 0,5 A for 2 minutes. The charge that passes is:
By convention, the current in a circuit diagram is drawn:
options: From the positive terminal through the circuit to the negative terminal
From the negative terminal through the circuit to the positive terminal

subtopics.title: Potential Difference, emf and the Energy Story

questions.question: Potential difference is defined as the work done per unit charge, and one volt equals:
A battery does 24 J of work driving 4 C of charge through itself. Its potential difference is:
The emf of a battery is the voltage across its terminals measured:
options: When no current flows — the open-circuit reading

questions.question: A battery goes flat because:
options: Its chemical energy is used up — the charge itself is never consumed
Its charge leaks into the air
The electrons in the circuit are consumed by the bulb

subtopics.title: Reading the Circuit — Ammeters and Voltmeters

questions.question: An ammeter is connected in ______ and has a ______ resistance.
A voltmeter is built with a very high resistance so that:
options: Only a trickle of current diverts through it, leaving the circuit undisturbed

questions.question: To measure the potential difference across a torch bulb, the voltmeter's two leads are placed:
options: Both on the battery's positive terminal
In line with the bulb, interrupting the loop
One on each side of the bulb, bridging it

questions.question: With a multi-scale meter, you should first connect to:
options: The largest scale, so the needle cannot be slammed past its limit

subtopics.title: Resistance — the Opposition in the Wire

questions.question: One ohm is defined as:
A bulb carries 0,5 A with 6 V across it. Its resistance is:
Microscopically, resistance arises because drifting electrons:
options: Repel each other out of the wire
Collide with vibrating ions of the metal lattice, transferring kinetic energy as heat

questions.question: Which change DECREASES the resistance of a wire?
In the water picture of a circuit, the pump, the water and the flow rate stand for:
options: The switch, the wires and the meter
The battery, the charge and the current
The bulb, the energy and the volts
The resistance, the current and the charge

questions.question: A battery does not create charge because:
options: Charge is created in the bulb instead
The charge is already in the wires — the battery just sets it moving

questions.question: An ampere is best described as:
options: A rate — one coulomb passing a point per second

questions.question: The same battery is connected first to a clogged, narrow circuit, then to a clear, wide one. The current:
options: Is the same both times — batteries fix the amps
Is larger in the clogged circuit
Differs: the circuit, not the battery, decides the flow

questions.question: A 6 V battery loads every coulomb with:
Sixty coulombs pass through a heater with 12 V across it. The energy delivered is:
Comparing the sticker reading with the switch off and the working reading with the switch on:
options: The emf reads slightly higher than the terminal potential difference
The terminal pd reads higher than the emf
Both read zero when current flows

questions.question: A flat battery is best described as:
options: Out of chemical energy to load onto the charge

subtopics.title: Clogs, Meters and the Kettle's Secret

questions.question: A kettle's element is made of high-resistance nichrome wire because:
options: The collisions there dump heat exactly where it is wanted
It prevents any current from flowing

questions.question: Which pair of changes both INCREASE a wire's resistance?
options: Copper instead of nichrome, and shorter

questions.question: The memory rule for the two meters is:
options: Ammeter in the loop for current through; voltmeter across the gap for volts across
Voltmeter in the loop; ammeter across the component

questions.question: Connecting an ammeter directly across a battery is dangerous because its very low resistance:
options: Turns the battery into a magnet
Creates a short circuit with a huge current through the meter
